question: Where can I get a list of active mines and quarries in the United States, with location, mineral or rock extracted, operator and annual production?

answer.summary: MSHA's weekly Mines file is the national list: 6,671 mines with Active status (6,096 metal/non-metal including stone, sand and gravel; 575 coal) with coordinates, operator, county and primary commodity; 6,492 of them reported work hours in 2025. Annual production per mine is published only for coal (its 2025 total matches EIA's 527.6 million short tons); quarries have hours but no tonnage. Pennsylvania DEP lists tons for 898 noncoal mines (2025).
main_caveats: MSHA 'Active' is a registry status, not proof of extraction: 6,492 of 6,671 Active mines reported hours in 2025, but so did 4,672 Intermittent and 745 Abandoned mines.
MSHA ANNUAL_COAL_PROD holds coal only; its unit is not in the definition file (its 2025 sum equals EIA's 527.6 million short tons).
Quarry and metal mines appear in the MSHA production file with hours and employees; ANNUAL_COAL_PROD is nonzero in only 113 non-coal rows over 2000-2026.
Pennsylvania repeats the same tonnage across permits of one site and its site rows sum to 103,947,203 tons against a printed total of 103,945,203.
MSHA 'Facility' mines (482 Active) are mills or plants, and 1,171 Active mines are portable operations, so a point may not be the pit.
State registries (CA SMARA, NV) record permit or operator-reported status; California says it cannot guarantee operator-reported coordinates.
answer.confidence_reason: MSHA, Pennsylvania and California files were downloaded and counted and coal totals matched EIA; USGS NMIC and most states were not opened.

attributes.note: MSHA Mines.txt: lat/lon for 6,659 of 6,671 Active mines (mostly 6 decimals); CA DMR 749 active and NV 157 points. Points only, no boundaries.
MSHA PRIMARY_SIC and PRIMARY_CANVASS (e.g. Construction Sand and Gravel, 2,123 active mines); PA 'Mineral'; CA PriProduct; NV COMMODITY.
MSHA CURRENT_OPERATOR_NAME on all 6,671 Active mines (3,561 operator ids) plus controller; CA Operator, PA Company, NV OPERATOR.
Coal: MSHA ANNUAL_COAL_PROD per mine (524 mines in 2024). Noncoal: PA DEP tons for 898 mines (2025); MSHA gives quarries only hours.
attributes.gap_note: No national per-mine tonnage for stone, sand, gravel or metals in MSHA, the CA DMR CSV or the NV layer. USGS NMIC facility data and other states were not opened.

sources.name: MSHA Open Government Data: Mines and Mine Employment/Production (yearly)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA)
sources.format: Zip of pipe-delimited text (Latin-1) with separate definition files; companion MinesProdYearly.zip
sources.license: Unknown (not stated on the pages opened)
sources.summary: National register of coal and metal/non-metal mines with status, operator, county, primary commodity and coordinates; yearly hours per mine and coal tonnage only for coal.
sources.coverage_note: Mines.txt of 2026-11-23: 92,129 rows, 6,671 Active (6,096 metal/non-metal, 575 coal).
caveats: Active status is not proof of extraction in the year.
Quarries have no production tonnage, only hours and employees.

example.example_request: curl -sL -o Mines.zip https://arlweb.msha.gov/OpenGovernmentData/DataSets/Mines.zip  # unzip; read Mines.txt with delimiter '|' and encoding latin-1; keep CURRENT_MINE_STATUS == 'Active'. Production: https://arlweb.msha.gov/OpenGovernmentData/DataSets/MinesProdYearly.zip, sum ANNUAL_COAL_PROD by MINE_ID and CALENDAR_YR.
example.example_result: Mines.txt: MINE_ID 0100003, O'Neal Quarry & Mill, Surface, Active since 01/22/1979, AL, Shelby, PRIMARY_SIC Lime, PRIMARY_CANVASS Stone, LATITUDE 33.177778, LONGITUDE -86.758889. MinesProdYearly 2025: Oak Grove Mine (0100851) ANNUAL_HRS 925328, ANNUAL_COAL_PROD 2394204.

sources.name: Pennsylvania industrial minerals mines reporting production, 2025 (listed by county)
sources.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Mining Programs
sources.format: XLSX (also PDF and an XLS statewide summary)
sources.license: Unknown (not stated in the files or folder)
sources.summary: Per-mine annual tons for 898 Pennsylvania noncoal mines in 2025 with mineral, company, permit and county, as XLSX.
sources.coverage_note: One state; no coordinates; county grouping only.
caveats: Subtotal and total rows are mixed with site rows.
Tonnage repeats across permits of the same site.

example.example_request: curl -sL -O https://files.dep.state.pa.us/Mining/BureauOfMiningPrograms/BMPPortalFiles/Annual_Reports/IndustrialAnnualReports/2025/2025IndustrialMineralsMines_ListedbyCounty.xlsx  # read sheet1: header row 6 (Company, Permit, Site Name, Acres, Production, Mineral, ...), county names in column A
example.example_result: Adams County, permit 01740601, Gettysburg Quarry, 113 acres, Production 193414, Mineral Hornfels, 47 employees, 9761 hours. Statewide Totals row: 898 mines, 103,945,203 tons.

sources.name: State active-mine layers: California DMR All Mines and Nevada NBMG Active Mines
sources.publisher: California Department of Conservation, Division of Mine Reclamation; Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology (University of Nevada, Reno)
sources.format: CSV, GeoJSON, KML, shapefile and WFS (California); ArcGIS REST JSON (Nevada)
sources.license: Unknown (not stated on the pages opened)
sources.summary: State layers listing regulated mines with status, operator and product (California 749 active, Nevada 157), without production.
sources.coverage_note: Two states queried; ids differ from MSHA ids.

members_summary.scope_note: Universe is every state mining or reclamation agency (about 50); two were queried and both lack production tonnage. Pennsylvania is a separate source because it publishes per-mine tons.
members_summary.pattern: Search '<state> mine reclamation active mines GIS' or '<state> annual mining report production by mine'.

if_unstructured.summary: Per-mine annual production for noncoal quarries outside Pennsylvania was not found as structured data in the sources opened; some states publish it in annual reports.

local_terms.meaning: Mine Safety and Health Administration, issues the 7-digit mine id.
MSHA class that includes stone, sand, gravel and other nonmetal mines.

local_terms.meaning: Forms from which MSHA mine name, operator and status are taken.
California Surface Mining and Reclamation Act of 1975.

2,000 lb unit used by EIA for coal; MSHA does not state a unit.
